# Syntax Characters as Plain Text

## Hash at start of line (not a heading)

# not heading

## Number-dot at start (not an ordered list)

1986. year of the Chernobyl disaster

## Dash at start (not a bullet)

- not list

## Escaped dash

\---

## Greater-than at start (not a quote)

> not quote

## Four-space indent (not a code block if inside a list — but here at top level it becomes one)

    this line has four spaces

## URL with underscores and query string

Visit http://example.com/a_b_c?x=1&y=2 for details.

## Asterisks that look like emphasis but are not

5 * 3 = 15 and 2 * 4 = 8

## Underscores that look like emphasis but are not

file_name_with_underscores.txt

## Brackets that look like links but are not

array[0] and array[1]

## Backticks that look like code but are not

The character ` alone is a grave accent.

## Caret and tilde

x^2 + y^2 = z^2

~tilde~ and ~~double tilde~~

## Slash that looks like a command

/help is not a command here.

## The full set on one line

# hash, - dash, > quote, * star, _ underscore, [ bracket, ` backtick, \ backslash

## End

Regular paragraph to close the file.
